events.description: Zia dismisses Prime Minister and National Assembly, abrogating progress toward democracy
Ambassador Dean cables State urging that AWACS sale discussions be held in abeyance until Zia shows commitment to democracy
Zia dismisses his Prime Minister and National Assembly, abrogating Pakistan's democratic progress.
Ambassador Dean cables Washington urging that discussion of AWACS sale to Pakistan be suspended until Zia shows by deed a commitment to democracy.

relationships.detail: Ambassador cabling the Secretary of State.
relationships.quote: FM AMEMBASSY NEW DELHI ... RUEHC / SECSTATE WASHDC IMMEDIATE

relationships.detail: Dean approved the cable for the embassy.
The cable from the New Delhi embassy was sent to SECSTATE Washington, marked immediate.
relationships.quote: FM AMEMBASSY NEW DELHI ... RUEHC / SECSTATE WASHDC IMMEDIATE 3587

relationships.detail: Dean approved the cable as ambassador, writing on behalf of the New Delhi embassy.
Dean criticizes Zia's dismissal of the government and urges that AWACS discussion be held in abeyance until Zia demonstrates a democratic commitment.
relationships.quote: ANY FURTHER DISCUSSION OF AWACS BE HELD IN ABEYANCE ... FOR AS LONG AS IT TAKES FOR ZIA TO DEMONSTRATE BY DEED HIS COMMITMENT

relationships.detail: The cable was sent to the Islamabad embassy and refers to its earlier cable (Ref A).
The cable was passed to USCINCCENT MacDill AFB via the Defense Department.
relationships.quote: DEPT PASS USCINCENT MACDILL AFB FL

relationships.detail: Zia is President of Pakistan and dismissed the Prime Minister and National Assembly.
relationships.quote: PRESIDENT ZIA ... BY DISMISSING HIS PRIME MINISTER AND NATIONAL ASSEMBLY

relationships.detail: Congress faces difficulties over future security assistance and AWACS notification for Pakistan after Zia's actions.
relationships.quote: DIFFICULTIES HE HAS CREATED FOR THE CONGRESS ON THE QUESTION OF FUTURE U.S. SECURITY ASSISTANCE TO PAKISTAN

relationships.detail: The US and Pakistan share a common victory over the Soviets in Afghanistan serving both countries' interests.
relationships.quote: OUR COMMON VICTORY OVER THE SOVIETS IN AFGHANISTAN SERVES BOTH U.S. AND PAKISTANI INTERESTS

key_claims: Dean argues Zia's dismissal of his PM and National Assembly complicates congressional support for security assistance to Pakistan.
Dean says AWACS notification after the dismissal would damage US credibility as a champion of democracy and human rights.
Dean says the common victory over the Soviets in Afghanistan does not oblige the US to overlook divergent interests with Pakistan.
Dean reports pervasive skepticism in India and the region about Zia's election promises.
Dean urges holding AWACS discussions in abeyance until Zia shows by deed a commitment to democratic government.
